PG 17 §5.5.5: "A foreign key constraint specifies that the values in a column (or a group of columns) must match the values appearing in some row of another table." ... "NO ACTION means that if any referencing rows still exist when the constraint is checked, an error is raised; this is the default behavior if you do not specify anything." schema.sql:28 specifies no ON DELETE action.

PG 17 §22.1: "It is not possible to access more than one database per connection." §5.10: "the even more general syntax database.schema.table can be used too, but at present this is just for pro forma compliance with the SQL standard. If you write a database name, it must be the same as the database you are connected to." A REFERENCES target is a table name, so it cannot name a table in another database. The literal phrase "cross-database references are not implemented" was not seen on these pages.

EF Core SQL Queries: "Entity Framework Core allows you to drop down to SQL queries when working with a relational database." SqlQuery "allows you to easily query for scalar, non-entity types via SQL"; the result type "does not need to match any table in the database". The SQL is passed as an interpolated string, which the C# compiler treats as text, so table/column names in it are first checked by the database when the query runs.

CatalogService.cs:5-8 "one product at a time goes through IProductRepository, which is the ProductCache (CatalogModule)"; FindAsync calls `products.FindAsync(id)`. CatalogModule.cs:38-42 registers IProductRepository as `new ProductCache(provider.GetRequiredService<EfProductRepository>(), ...)`. Note ListAsync reads CatalogDbContext directly; the lesson's "such as" wording is compatible.
